# Environment of the API. Export these variables (or set them in your IDE) before running it. Never commit real values.

# Port the API listens on
PORT=8080

# Secret that signs the tokens of your identity provider (at least 32 bytes). Without it every protected request is rejected.

# Optional: expected audience and issuer of the tokens

JWT_ISSUER=

files.README.md:
# library-api

REST API generated by [Model2API](https://raulesteveza.github.io/tools/Model2API/) with Ktor. It is a starting point: review it before using it in production.

## Run it

Requires Java 21 and Gradle 9 (or a Gradle wrapper: `gradle wrapper` creates one).

```bash
gradle run
```

Set the variables of `.env.example` in your environment first. The API listens on http://localhost:8080. Its contract is in `openapi.yaml`.

## Test it

```bash
gradle test
```

Each test starts the application anew, so it starts with empty storage.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does | Success | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/authors` | List authors | 200 | public |
| `GET` | `/authors/{id}` | Get an author | 200 | public |
| `POST` | `/authors` | Create an author | 201 | public |
| `PUT` | `/authors/{id}` | Replace an author | 200 | public |
| `PATCH` | `/authors/{id}` | Update part of an author | 200 | public |
| `DELETE` | `/authors/{id}` | Delete an author | 204 | public |
| `PUT` | `/archive/{id}` | Business operation | 202 | public |
| `GET` | `/books` | List books | 200 | public |
| `GET` | `/books/{id}` | Get a book | 200 | public |
| `POST` | `/books` | Create a book | 201 | public |
| `PUT` | `/books/{id}` | Replace a book | 200 | public |
| `PATCH` | `/books/{id}` | Update part of a book | 200 | public |
| `DELETE` | `/books/{id}` | Delete a book | 204 | public |

Errors always have the same body: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...]}}`. Invalid requests answer 400.

## Storage

Data is kept in memory while the application runs and is lost when it stops. Write another implementation of each repository interface and create it in `Application.kt`.

## Authentication

Protected endpoints need a bearer token issued by your identity provider, signed with HS256. The API verifies it with `JWT_SECRET` (and `JWT_AUDIENCE` / `JWT_ISSUER` when set), requires an expiry, and reads the roles from the `roles` claim. It does not issue tokens.

## Structure

```text
src/main/kotlin/com/example/api/
  Application.kt        entry point: wires storage, services and routes
  common/               errors, request bodies, JSON, lists and settings
  model/                domain classes, enums and embedded objects
  dto/                  request bodies and responses
  repository/           storage
  service/              rules of each resource
  routes/               HTTP routes
  security/             authentication
src/test/kotlin/         one test class per resource
openapi.yaml             the contract of the API
```

## Left to you

- `PUT /archive/{id}` (Business operation): write its logic in the service; it answers 501 until then.

package com.example.api

import com.example.api.common.JsonFormat
import com.example.api.common.Settings
import com.example.api.common.installErrors
import com.example.api.repository.InMemoryAuthorRepository
import com.example.api.repository.InMemoryBookRepository
import com.example.api.routes.authorRoutes
import com.example.api.routes.bookRoutes
import com.example.api.security.installSecurity
import com.example.api.service.AuthorService
import com.example.api.service.BookService
import io.ktor.serialization.kotlinx.json.json
import io.ktor.server.application.Application
import io.ktor.server.application.install
import io.ktor.server.engine.embeddedServer
import io.ktor.server.netty.Netty
import io.ktor.server.plugins.contentnegotiation.ContentNegotiation
import io.ktor.server.routing.routing

/** Starts the API on PORT (8080 by default) with the settings of the environment. */
fun main() {
    val port = System.getenv("PORT")?.toIntOrNull() ?: 8080
    embeddedServer(Netty, port = port) { module(Settings.fromEnvironment()) }.start(wait = true)
}

/** The API: JSON, errors, authentication, storage and routes. */
fun Application.module(settings: Settings) {
    install(ContentNegotiation) { json(JsonFormat) }
    installErrors()
    installSecurity(settings)

    // Data kept in memory while the application runs; restarting it (or each test) starts empty
    val authorRepository = InMemoryAuthorRepository()
    val bookRepository = InMemoryBookRepository()
    val authorService = AuthorService(authorRepository)
    val bookService = BookService(bookRepository, authorRepository)

    routing {
        authorRoutes(authorService)
        bookRoutes(bookService)
    }
}

package com.example.api.dto

import com.example.api.common.Checks
import com.example.api.common.JsonDate
import com.example.api.common.JsonKind
import com.example.api.common.JsonUuid
import com.example.api.model.Genre
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject

/** Body of a request that creates or replaces a book. */
@Serializable
data class BookCreate(
    val title: String? = null,
    val isbn: String? = null,
    val authorId: JsonUuid? = null,
    val genre: Genre? = null,
    val pages: Int? = null,
    val published: JsonDate? = null,
    val available: Boolean? = null,
) {
    companion object {
        /** What the body must meet, checked on its JSON before it is read. */
        fun rules(checks: Checks, json: JsonObject) {
            checks.required(json, "title")
            checks.notNull(json, "title")
            checks.kind(json, "title", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.length(json, "title", 1, 200)
            checks.required(json, "isbn")
            checks.notNull(json, "isbn")
            checks.kind(json, "isbn", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.pattern(json, "isbn", Regex("^[0-9]{13}\$"))
            checks.required(json, "authorId")
            checks.notNull(json, "authorId")
            checks.kind(json, "authorId", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "genre")
            checks.notNull(json, "genre")
            checks.kind(json, "genre", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.required(json, "pages")
            checks.notNull(json, "pages")
            checks.kind(json, "pages", JsonKind.WHOLE)
            checks.range(json, "pages", "1", "5000", false, false)
            checks.kind(json, "published", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.pattern(json, "published", Regex("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\$"))
            checks.notNull(json, "available")
            checks.kind(json, "available", JsonKind.BOOLEAN)
        }
    }
}

package com.example.api.dto

import com.example.api.common.JsonDate
import com.example.api.common.JsonUuid
import com.example.api.model.Book
import com.example.api.model.Genre
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/** A book as the API returns it. */
@Serializable
data class BookResponse(
    val id: JsonUuid,
    val title: String?,
    val isbn: String?,
    val authorId: JsonUuid?,
    val genre: Genre?,
    val pages: Int?,
    val published: JsonDate?,
    val available: Boolean?,
) {
    companion object {
        /** The response of a stored book: everything but what clients only send. */
        fun from(item: Book) = BookResponse(
            id = item.id,
            title = item.title,
            isbn = item.isbn,
            authorId = item.authorId,
            genre = item.genre,
            pages = item.pages,
            published = item.published,
            available = item.available,
        )
    }
}
